meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have until 4:40, Hale, so let's not waste it. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.
You didn't answer my question, but fine. 11:52 PM on what date, and whose version history? Turn the screen so I can read it myself.
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.

"Maybe." My happiness isn't the standard, Hale, so either the evidence holds or it doesn't. If the zero is coming off, I want that in an email today, with confirmation that nothing about this is on Owen's record.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In our meeting today you said you would remove the zero from Owen's essay. I still require written confirmation that the zero is withdrawn and that nothing about this matter is on Owen's record. I expect that email from you today.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing formally agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn in writing and confirmation that nothing is on Owen's record.
What moved her: "612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM" made her stop attacking and ask to see the document, because it was specific and tied to Owen's own work, though it had no date.
What cost ground: "maybe I'm wrong about all this" dropped your own evidence the moment she pushed, and "if that makes you happy" made the mark sound like a favour instead of a decision.
Try next time: when she asked for the date and to see the screen, give her the date, show her the version history, and first own in one sentence that the zero went in before anyone called her.
